topics.label: Course introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: It frames the lecture series by introducing the scope of cancer biology, the student cohort, and the core learning outcomes.

topics.label: Fundamental concepts of cancer development and tissue architecture
topics.groupedBecause: They establish the core definition of cancer as an accumulation of genetic alterations leading to a failure of cellular differentiation and tissue architecture, alongside the experimental models used to study these processes.

topics.label: Invasion, metastasis, and the distinction between benign and malignant tumors
topics.groupedBecause: They explain how invasion and metastasis distinguish malignant from benign neoplasms, illustrating the stepwise progression and clinical behavior of tumors.

topics.label: Conventions and exceptions in tumor nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: It defines the standard pathological naming conventions and key exceptions used to classify benign and malignant tumors across different tissue origins.

topics.label: Pathophysiological mechanisms of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: It details the mechanical and systemic ways in which primary and metastatic tumors impair organ function to cause illness and death.

topics.label: Tumor incidence and comparative oncology across species
topics.groupedBecause: They examine the patterns of cancer incidence and mortality across human populations and other multicellular organisms.

topics.label: Principles, implementation, and limitations of cancer screening
topics.groupedBecause: They evaluate the clinical strategies, histological markers, and practical limitations of screening for early-stage and precursor lesions in various cancers.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical reminders
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture with a review of the learning outcomes and administrative reminders for upcoming practicals and lectures.
